Check transit service availability by date

Source: R/network_tools.R
check_transit_availability.Rd

Counts the public transport services in the GTFS feeds of a network that are active on given dates, and their proportion of all services. Use it to pick a departure date with adequate service: public transport routing only finds trips on dates when services run (per the GTFS calendars and date exceptions).

Usage

check_transit_availability(
  network,
  dates = NULL,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL
)

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network().

dates

A vector of specific dates to be checked. Can be character strings in "YYYY-MM-DD" format, or objects of class Date. This argument cannot be used with start_date or end_date. Defaults to NULL; when all date arguments are NULL, operating dates are discovered from the network.

start_date

The start date for a continuous date range. Must be a single character string in "YYYY-MM-DD" format or a Date object. Must be used with end_date.

end_date

The end date for a continuous date range. Must be a single character string in "YYYY-MM-DD" format or a Date object. Must be used with start_date.

Value

A table with four columns: date (Date), total_services, active_services and pct_active (the proportion of active services). Automatic discovery returns dates in ascending order, or a zero-row table with these columns if no retained transit trips operate.

Details

When no date arguments are supplied, the function discovers all dates with an active service referenced by a retained transit trip, including frequency-based trips. This accounts for weekday calendars and date exceptions, including exception-only services. A date with active service does not guarantee a trip at every departure time or between every pair of points.

You can also specify the dates to check in two ways: a vector of specific dates in dates, or a continuous range with start_date and end_date. You cannot combine these methods. In all modes, total_services counts every imported service, not only those used by trips; counts are of services, not trips. If calendar bounds are invalid, automatic discovery fails naming the service; explicit date queries remain available.

See also

Other network functions: build_network(), find_snap(), get_gtfs_errors(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf(), transit_network_to_sf()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
head(check_transit_availability(network))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   date       total_services active_services pct_active
#>   <date>              <int>           <int>      <dbl>
#> 1 2008-01-01              6               3      0.5  
#> 2 2008-01-02              6               3      0.5  
#> 3 2008-01-03              6               3      0.5  
#> 4 2008-01-04              6               3      0.5  
#> 5 2008-01-05              6               4      0.667
#> 6 2008-01-06              6               3      0.5  
check_transit_availability(network, dates = c("2019-05-13", "2019-05-19"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   date       total_services active_services pct_active
#>   <date>              <int>           <int>      <dbl>
#> 1 2019-05-13              6               3        0.5
#> 2 2019-05-19              6               3        0.5
